For fixed x in {3,..,8}, the same inequalities give the exact y-range x<=y<=6x/(x-2) and 1/y < 1/2-1/x, so the feasible pairs are exactly the finite list { (3,3),(3,4),(3,5),(3,6),(3,7),(3,8),(3,9),(3,10),(3,11),(3,12),(3,13),(3,14),(3,15),(3,16),(3,17),(3,18),(4,4),(4,5),(4,6),(4,7),(4,8),(4,9),(4,10),(4,11),(4,12),(5,5),(5,6),(5,7),(5,8),(5,9),(5,10),(6,6),(6,7),(6,8),(6,9),(7,7),(7,8),(8,8) }, omitting (5,5) and (8,8) because they violate 1/y < 1/2 - 1/x; the true count is 35. child_packets.account: LEMMA (proved here in full; children supplied derivations but no sources). Let p,q be coprime positive integers. The map (z,w) -> (u,v) = (pz-q, pw-q) is a bijection from positive integer solutions of 1/z + 1/w = p/q with z <= w onto pairs (u,v) of positive integers with uv = q^2, 1 <= u <= v, and u ≡ -q (mod p); the congruence v ≡ -q (mod p) is automatic. FORWARD: 1/z+1/w = p/q iff q(z+w) = pzw (multiply by qzw, exact). Multiply by p and rearrange: p^2 zw - pqz - pqw + q^2 = q^2, i.e. (pz-q)(pw-q) = q^2. Since 1/w > 0 gives 1/z < p/q, we get pz > q, so u = pz-q >= 1; likewise v >= 1. The congruences hold by construction and z <= w iff u <= v (child A, C004). INVERSE: given uv = q^2, 1 <= u <= v, u ≡ v ≡ -q (mod p), set z = (u+q)/p, w = (v+q)/p. The congruences make z,w integers; u+q is a positive multiple of p hence >= p, so z >= 1, likewise w >= 1, and u <= v gives z <= w. Expanding (pz-q)(pw-q) = q^2 yields p^2 zw = pq(z+w), hence q(z+w) = pzw, hence 1/z+1/w = p/q on division by pzw > 0. The two maps are two-sided inverses (child A, C005). AUTOMATIC v-CONGRUENCE: if uv = q^2 and u ≡ -q (mod p), then q(v+q) ≡ 0 (mod p); coprimality makes q a unit mod p, so v ≡ -q. Only one congruence per divisor need be checked. COUNTING FORMULA: since u <= v with uv = q^2 iff u <= q <= v, N(p,q) = #{u in Z+ : u | q^2, 1 <= u <= q, u ≡ -q (mod p)}, each u yielding exactly one solution (z,w) = ((u+q)/p, (q^2/u + q)/p). The extra bound z >= y becomes, via z = (u+q)/p with p > 0, exactly u >= py - q, so the filtered count is N(p,q;y) = #{u | q^2 : u ≡ -q (mod p), max(1, py-q) <= u <= q} — a hand-checkable divisor scan of q^2. WORKED EXAMPLE (p=1, q=2; child C): q^2 = 4 and the congruence is mod 1, hence vacuous. Divisors u of 4 with 1 <= u <= 2 are u = 1, 2. u=1: v=4, (z,w) = (3,6); check 1/3+1/6 = 2/6+1/6 = 1/2. u=2: v=2, (z,w) = (4,4); check 1/4+1/4 = 1/2. Count = 2 exactly. Excluded: z = 2 gives u = 0 (would force 1/w = 0); z = 1 gives u = -1 < 0 (would force 1/w = -1/2); the lemma's bound z > q/p = 2 captures both. CONFLICT RESOLVED per policy: child B's specialization p = xy-x-y, q = x+y is inconsistent with the target equation; the correct reduction is 1/z+1/w = 1/2 - 1/x - 1/y = (xy - 2x - 2y)/(2xy), taken in lowest terms as p/q. CAVEAT: all three children derived the same algebra from the same node specification with no independent sources, so their agreement is correlated corroboration, not independent confirmation; the proof above stands on its own line-checkable algebra, which the acceptance condition permits.

claims.statement: Forward direction: for coprime p,q, if positive integers z,w satisfy 1/z + 1/w = p/q then (pz-q)(pw-q) = q^2, with u = pz-q >= 1, v = pw-q >= 1, u ≡ v ≡ -q (mod p), and z <= w iff u <= v; positivity of u,v follows from 1/z < p/q.

Inverse direction: every pair (u,v) of positive integers with uv = q^2, u <= v, u ≡ v ≡ -q (mod p) yields, via z = (u+q)/p and w = (v+q)/p, a positive integer solution of 1/z + 1/w = p/q with z <= w; u+q is a positive multiple of p hence >= p, so z >= 1; the two maps are two-sided inverses.

The congruence v ≡ -q (mod p) is automatic: from uv = q^2 and u ≡ -q (mod p) follows q(v+q) ≡ 0 (mod p), and coprimality gcd(p,q)=1 makes q invertible mod p, giving v ≡ -q; hence the counting scan only tests one congruence per divisor u.

Exact counting formula: the number of solutions with z <= w is N(p,q) = #{u positive : u divides q^2, 1 <= u <= q, u ≡ -q (mod p)}; each admissible u determines v = q^2/u >= u and exactly one solution (z,w) = ((u+q)/p, (v+q)/p).

Filter for z >= y: since p > 0, z >= y iff u >= py - q, so the filtered count is N(p,q;y) = #{u | q^2 : u ≡ -q (mod p), max(1, py-q) <= u <= q}; filtering is a finite divisor scan of q^2 requiring no floating-point arithmetic.

Worked example p=1, q=2: q^2 = 4, congruence mod 1 vacuous, admissible divisors u in [1,2] are 1 and 2, giving factor pairs (1,4) and (2,2) and exactly the solutions (z,w) = (3,6) and (4,4); exact checks 1/3+1/6 = 1/2 and 1/4+1/4 = 1/2; count = 2.

Exclusion in the example: z = 2 corresponds to u = 0 and z = 1 to u = -1, both violating u >= 1; equivalently they would force 1/w = 0 and 1/w = -1/2 respectively, impossible for positive integer w; the lemma's bound z > q/p = 2 captures this.

Correction of child B's specialization: 1/z + 1/w = 1/2 - 1/x - 1/y = (xy - 2x - 2y)/(2xy), so p/q must be that fraction reduced to lowest terms; child B's p = xy - x - y, q = x + y (which equals (1/x + 1/y) - style numerator) contradicts the exact identity and must not be used in the parent's table.

counterevidence: Child B (C001) stated the specialization p = xy - x - y, q = x + y; direct expansion of 1/2 - 1/x - 1/y gives (xy - 2x - 2y)/(2xy), so B's formula is rejected in favor of the exact identity per the conflict policy.

source_materials.content:
Determine the exact number of quadruples of positive integers

\[
x \le y \le z \le w
\]

satisfying

\[
\frac1x+\frac1y+\frac1z+\frac1w=\frac12.
\]

Give a self-contained rigorous proof that the count is complete. Include an
auditable table giving the number of solutions for every feasible pair
\((x,y)\), together with row totals for each \(x\) and the grand total. Derive
finite bounds and use exact arithmetic throughout. A factor-pair or divisor
enumeration lemma for the final two denominators is welcome. The final answer
need not print every quadruple, but its table and method must be detailed enough
for a reader to reproduce the count without trusting a brute-force program.
